title: Render the review substrate as a live workflow graph
description: Replace the static HTML review layout with a read-only React Flow canvas composed from the Vercel AI Elements workflow primitives. Stream cross-process SQLite changes over WebSocket and retain polling as disconnect recovery. Non-goals: graph editing, collaborative cursors, remote persistence, and replacing the existing domain or MCP authority.

behaviors.title: Render one deterministic workflow graph from the complete issue substrate
behaviors.trigger: A builder opens an issue in the visualizer
behaviors.expected: The canvas shows the issue, behaviors, evidence, findings, three review passes, and terminal shipping disposition as connected typed nodes
behaviors.verify: Open a seeded issue in a real browser and inspect the accessible graph for every substrate class and the exact hold disposition

behaviors.title: Keep the workflow canvas inspectable but read-only
behaviors.trigger: A builder pans, zooms, selects, or focuses workflow nodes
behaviors.expected: Navigation and detail inspection work without exposing node deletion, arbitrary movement, or connection mutations
behaviors.verify: Exercise canvas controls and keyboard focus in a real browser, then confirm the substrate database is unchanged

behaviors.title: Stream cross-process substrate changes to the open graph
behaviors.trigger: A separate CLI or MCP process commits a change to the visualizer's SQLite database
behaviors.expected: The server detects the SQLite version change, broadcasts a WebSocket event, and the open graph updates without manual refresh
behaviors.verify: Keep DEMO-1 open in a real browser, mutate it through a separate built CLI process, and observe the displayed review state change within two seconds

behaviors.title: Recover live state through polling when WebSocket is unavailable
behaviors.trigger: The WebSocket disconnects while the visualizer remains open
behaviors.expected: The client shows degraded connection state and interval polling still converges the graph to the latest substrate
behaviors.verify: Block or close the WebSocket, mutate the database through a separate process, and observe the browser update through the polling fallback

behaviors.title: Preserve existing Loopbreaker authority and demo actions
behaviors.trigger: A builder records pass two, adds wired proof, or accepts named debt from the new visualizer
behaviors.expected: The existing domain functions remain the only mutation authority and review stays separate from shipping
behaviors.verify: Run the complete repository verification suite and exercise review-complete plus hold followed by wired-proof plus ship in a real browser

planning.outcome: Builders can inspect the complete review substrate as a live workflow graph.
planning.appetite: One focused visualizer and realtime transport slice.

work_units.title: Build and wire the realtime workflow canvas
work_units.done_when: The production browser renders and refreshes the read-only substrate through both transports.

proofs.method: Inspect the complete accessible graph in a real browser.
Exercise canvas navigation and compare substrate hashes.
Mutate with a separate CLI process and observe WebSocket refresh.
Disconnect the server and observe polling plus reconnect catch-up.
Run the full suite and demo hold-to-ship transition.

planning.production_wiring: Serve the Vite bundle and WebSocket from the production Node HTTP entry point backed by SQLite data-version detection.
planning.rollback: Restore the static view while preserving the existing domain, CLI, MCP, and SQLite data.
planning.migration: Replace generated web assets; no domain-data migration is required.

risks.risk: A disconnected client misses an invalidation.
risks.mitigation: Reload on reconnect and retain polling recovery.
